title: Shadow Hearts
subtitle: An uneasy journey through 1913
summary: Shadow Hearts is Sacnoth's PlayStation 2 role-playing game, first released in Japan on 28 June 2001. Yuri Hyuga can transform into monsters, a power that draws him into the struggle surrounding Alice Elliot and a dangerous magician. Their journey crosses a fictional version of the early twentieth century where recognisable places coexist with supernatural threats. The party explores towns and hostile locations, then fights in turn-based encounters. Its combination of historical surroundings, disturbing creatures and eccentric companions gives the adventure a markedly different atmosphere from a conventional fantasy quest.
body: Shadow Hearts is Sacnoth's PlayStation 2 role-playing game, first released in Japan on 28 June 2001. Yuri Hyuga can transform into monsters, a power that draws him into the struggle surrounding Alice Elliot and a dangerous magician. Their journey crosses a fictional version of the early twentieth century where recognisable places coexist with supernatural threats. The party explores towns and hostile locations, then fights in turn-based encounters. Its combination of historical surroundings, disturbing creatures and eccentric companions gives the adventure a markedly different atmosphere from a conventional fantasy quest.

Choosing an attack is only the beginning of a turn. A rotating indicator crosses marked sections of the Judgement Ring, and the player presses a button as it reaches the appropriate areas. Accurate timing determines whether the selected action succeeds and how well it works. The same idea extends beyond basic weapon attacks, keeping attention on the screen while the party takes its turns. Character abilities and equipment still require planning, but the ring makes execution something the player must perform rather than simply confirm.

Yuri's Fusion ability allows him to take on different monstrous forms, giving the party another set of powers to manage. The setting continues the world of Sacnoth's earlier Koudelka, with recurring connections beneath the new journey. Director and writer Matsuzo Machida drew on horror fiction and manga, while Yoshitaka Hirota's score mixed musical styles to support the unsettling tone. Reviewers responded to the story and timing system more warmly than to every part of the presentation. Shadow Hearts: Covenant continued Yuri's story in 2004.
